sequence_description: Baseline: two local password users map to distinct identities. Attack: SAML login with attacker-controlled principal but victim's email (email_verified=false) should NOT link to victim.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_saml_entity_id != user_A_entity_id
Evaluation: user_attacker_saml_entity_id='crjeedqw0w1n' != 'crjeedqw0w1n' → False
Implication: SAML principal with email_verified=false was mapped/linked to the local victim account (account takeover via unverified email linking)

sequence_description: Baseline: two local password users map to distinct identities. Attack: SAML logins with same email differing only by case should not collapse into the same downstream identity if treated as security-distinct upstream principals.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_case_1_entity_id != user_case_2_entity_id
Evaluation: user_case_1_entity_id='r7j1sq8fdik5' != 'r7j1sq8fdik5' → False
Implication: Two security-distinct upstream SAML principals (different sub) collapsed into the same downstream identity due to case normalization/ambiguous email matching

sequence_description: Cross-protocol identity merge attempt: existing local password user, then SAML login presents same email with different case and different upstream sub; should not collapse into the same downstream identity (unless explicitly linked).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_saml_casefold_login_status >= 400 OR user_attacker_saml_casefold_entity_id != user_A_entity_id
Evaluation: (user_attacker_saml_casefold_login_status=200 >= 400 → False) OR (user_attacker_saml_casefold_entity_id='vvonxetswd4y' != 'vvonxetswd4y' → False)
Implication: SAML principal with case-variant email collapsed/linked to existing local password identity (account merge/collision)

sequence_description: Cross-issuer principal collision: two SAML logins use the same upstream sub/email but different SAML Issuer (idp_entity_id). They are security-distinct principals and must not collapse into one downstream identity.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_saml_issuer_A_login_status >= 400 OR user_saml_issuer_B_login_status >= 400 OR user_saml_issuer_A_entity_id != user_saml_issuer_B_entity_id
Evaluation: ((user_saml_issuer_A_login_status=200 >= 400 → False) OR (user_saml_issuer_B_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)) OR (user_saml_issuer_A_entity_id='3mgwfy9amg6m' != '3mgwfy9amg6m' → False)
Implication: Two security-distinct SAML issuers with the same sub/email collapsed into the same downstream identity (issuer not bound)

evidence.assertion: user_saml_issuer_A_login_status >= 400 OR user_saml_issuer_B_login_status >= 400 OR user_saml_issuer_A_entity_id != user_saml_issuer_B_entity_id
